method: Thesis exposure = sum over open theses of posterior x value-pool weight (mandatory infrastructure 1.0, pricing power / scarce 0.9, abundant -0.3, new risk -0.6, loses pricing power -1.0). Final = exposure x (0.5 + opportunity/100) x (1 + gap/100) x technical readiness (trend template) x attention (not-priced +15%, crowded -20%). 'ready' = passes the book's entry gate today.

picks.why: Highest composite score (6.66) and the only name in the set that is both technically ready (stage2, score 100) and not being over-charged for its thesis load \u2014 expectations gap +3 with pricing 68 against reality 70. It sits at the intersection of four pools: endpoint inference silicon and trust/attestation for local inference (T-004, posterior 97.5), on-device health telemetry and adherence agents (T-005, 87.8), agentic interfaces to finance (T-008, 80.3) and trusted delegation (T-001). The market prices it as a mature handset annuity, not as the attestation and on-device-inference toll booth four separate theses independently route value through; attention is only 31 and it is not crowded.
picks.entry_condition: Already buy-ready \u2014 take initial position while stage2 structure holds; add on an OS-level agent shipping with stored payment authority on by default (T-001 secondary tell) or a named non-diagnosed OTC sensor disclosure cycle.
picks.key_risk: T-001 posterior is the weakest in the book at 61.7; if the April 2027 network rulebook cycle passes with no agent-transaction liability standard, the delegation leg (1.73 of its 5.62 exposure) decays and the name reverts to a hardware-cycle multiple.

picks.why: The cheapest way to own the six-layer security cluster: identical thesis exposure (5.47) and identical role map to PANW and ZS, but an expectations gap of only -1 (pricing 79 vs reality 77) against PANW's -20 and CRWD's -19, with the highest opportunity score in the security group at 71. Technically ready, stage2, score 100, attention 40 and uncrowded. The market is paying a consolidation premium for PANW/CRWD narrative while Fortinet delivers the same mandatory-infrastructure exposure \u2014 enterprise platforms (T-002), trust and attestation (T-004), biometric data governance (T-005), custody/key management (T-008) \u2014 at near-fair expectations.
picks.entry_condition: Buy on the current stage2 structure; size up if agent-governance appears as a separately priced, attach-rate-disclosed line in Q4 FY2026/Q1 FY2027 security vendor disclosures (the single strongest T-002 confirmation available).
picks.key_risk: T-002's explicit falsifier \u2014 agent governance bundled free into platform deals \u2014 would confirm security deflation and hit the whole cluster; Fortinet also carries more hardware-refresh cyclicality than the pure-software comps, so a flat IT-spend year compresses it faster.

picks.why: Fairly priced exposure (gap -1, pricing 64 vs reality 63) to the single most reinforced scarcity in the book: skilled trades appear as 'scarce' or 'gains_pricing_power' in T-007 (90.2), T-006 (83.5), T-004 (97.5) and T-003 (80.0) simultaneously \u2014 four independent theses converging on crew-owning specialty contractors. Technically ready at 88, stage2, and it carries no narrative or attention score at all, which is exactly the profile of a value pool nobody has written the story for yet. FIX has the same role map and a better reality score but is in a basing structure; IESC is the one you can actually buy today.
picks.entry_condition: Enter on stage2 continuation; confirm on Q3 2026 specialty-contractor earnings showing backlog duration extending past 18 months with craft labour named as the binding constraint and explicit field-wage escalation clauses.
picks.key_risk: T-006's fastest falsifier \u2014 a neocloud or GPU-financing credit event, or a disclosed data-centre cancellation \u2014 turns scarcity rent into crew release within a quarter or two; small-cap liquidity means that repricing is violent.

picks.why: The largest raw thesis exposure in the entire candidate set (6.41) concentrated in the highest-posterior thesis in the book: T-004 at 97.5 contributes 2.73, T-003 at 80.0 adds 2.16, across power generation scarcity, SMR supply chain scarcity and grid orchestration software. Yet it is the only high-exposure name with a positive expectations gap (+7, pricing 54 vs reality 61) \u2014 the market has stopped paying for it even as the electrons-before-silicon mechanism became near-certain. Narrative 77 against pricing 54 is the clearest narrative-price divergence here.
picks.entry_condition: Do not buy the base \u2014 technical score 50, stage basing/downtrend, not ready. Wait for a confirmed stage2 transition, or for the T-004 primary signal: a top-five hyperscaler contracting firm generation before interconnection is granted on a >=1GW campus.
picks.key_risk: A first neocloud or vendor-financed GPU default shrinks the announcement pipeline that this entire backlog narrative rests on; T-004's own authors flag this as the invalidating event for the primary metric.

picks.why: The widest positive expectations gap among the power names (+10, pricing 43 vs reality 53) with 3.12 of its 5.36 exposure coming from T-004 at 97.5 posterior \u2014 firm dispatchable generation adjacent to load gaining pricing power, and powered land/interconnection/water rights becoming scarce. No narrative score and no attention reading at all: this is permission and powered land being valued as a leveraged utility balance sheet rather than as the scarcest input in AI buildout.
picks.entry_condition: Not ready (technical 62, emerging). Enter only on confirmed breakout out of the emerging stage, ideally coinciding with hard count data on local denials/moratoria citing power or water \u2014 T-004's least-evidenced leg (b), which is exactly what repricing permission requires.
picks.key_risk: T-004 explicitly flags community/ratepayer political risk as a new_risk layer for this exact exposure; AES also carries rate-sensitive leverage into a 5.3% 10-year, so the cheap pricing may be a correct balance-sheet judgement rather than a mispriced scarcity.

picks.why: Same 5.47 security-cluster exposure and same six mandatory-infrastructure roles as PANW and CRWD, but with a positive expectations gap (+6, pricing 54 vs reality 60) versus their -20 and -19. Narrative 78 matches the cluster leaders while pricing sits 30+ points below them \u2014 the market is discounting execution, not the thesis. This is the cheapest option on T-002, T-004 attestation and T-005 biometric governance all resolving favourably.
picks.entry_condition: Technical 62, emerging, not ready \u2014 wait for stage2 confirmation. Fundamental trigger: agent-governance disclosed as a separately priced line with attach rates in the Q4 FY2026/Q1 FY2027 cycle.
picks.key_risk: The pricing discount reflects reality 60 versus FTNT's 77 \u2014 if the gap is execution rather than sentiment, a correct thesis still produces a losing position as platform consolidation routes budget to PANW and CRWD.

picks.why: The lowest pricing score in the entire set (38) against a +11 expectations gap, with 2.25 of exposure to T-008 (posterior 80.3) via stablecoin issuance and reserve float as mandatory infrastructure, multi-venue brokerage permissioning, and agentic interfaces to finance as scarce \u2014 plus 2.22 to T-001 delegation. The market is pricing a structurally impaired checkout button and paying nothing for optionality on tokenised settlement rails, which no other candidate here provides at this valuation.
picks.entry_condition: Basing/downtrend, technical 50 \u2014 no entry on structure. Buy only on both a stage transition and a hard T-008 print: a top-five broker publishing tokenised-equity volume with named market makers, or a CCP/prime broker accepting a tokenised MMF as eligible margin.
picks.key_risk: It is the only name in the set carrying a negative headwind (-0.42) \u2014 T-009 casts payments rails as liability underwriters for elder scam losses, so the same thesis set that creates the upside also assigns it new uncompensated liability.

memo.portfolio_note: This is two engines plus one option book. Engine one is electrons and trades \u2014 IESC, GEV, AES \u2014 all drawing on T-004 at 97.5 posterior and T-006/T-007 skilled-labour scarcity; the exposures are highly correlated and share a single falsifier, a GPU-financing or neocloud credit event that converts backlog into released crews, so treat them as one position of roughly a third of risk, not three. Engine two is the security cluster, where the discipline is to own exposure at FTNT's -1 expectations gap and ZS's +6 rather than PANW's -20, CRWD's -19 or NET's -17 \u2014 identical role maps, wildly different prices, and a single shared binary (agent governance priced separately versus bundled free) that settles T-002. AAPL is the only name that bridges both the inference-trust and the delegation pools and is the sole buy-ready, fairly-priced, uncrowded candidate, which earns it the largest single weight. PYPL is a small option, not a core holding: cheapest pricing in the set but carrying the only negative headwind. Four of seven are not technically ready (GEV, AES, ZS, PYPL) and should sit as staged orders. The list changes if GPU spot rental rates fail to fall or a vendor-financed GPU default prints \u2014 that guts the power/trades engine and I would rotate weight into the security cluster and AAPL; conversely, if agent governance is bundled free in the Q4 FY2026 disclosures, FTNT and ZS come out and the power names take their weight.
